inconsistencies: Three PRs solve the same trace-logging configuration problem: #34038 (-trace), #35387 (standalone -loglevel + RPC) and #35355 (atomics + -trace + RPC). Review #34038 and #35387 together to settle the approach NACK first; #35355 should not be reviewed until that is decided.
#35355 and #35322 both replace the mutex-guarded category level map with atomic bitmasks; #35322 is the standalone version, so whichever lands first makes part of the other redundant.

ArgsManager chain, review in this order: #16545 (base) → #17580 → #17783 and #17493 → #17581. #16545 and #17493 both target duplicate config-file assignments; #16545's validation must be settled first.
util::Result chain: #25665 (base) → #26022 → #25722. #25722 is unreviewable in isolation.

Logging chain: #34778 (base, unresolved concept NACK) → #29256 → #30342 → #30343. The whole stack, including a tested-ACKed #30343, is stalled on the #34778 approach decision; that decision is the highest-value action in the logging sub-area.
#36278 (minisketch) and #36282 (leveldb) are both prerequisites of #36275 (-Wunused-const-variable); merging only one does not unblock it, so review them as a pair.
#36105 fixes Windows ExecVp; #36190 only adds the functional test for it and must follow.

#35676 deliberately makes low-level disk helpers abort() while #36049 removes an abort on buffered write failure; these push filesystem error handling in opposite directions and should be decided together.
#19460 was banded below #19461 even though it is its base and the same change for a different binary; corrected to the same band with #19460 first.

Silent payments overlap: #32966 (Receiving) predates the 'take 2' series (#35301 base, #35302 sending); confirm #32966 is not superseded before spending review time on it, and review #35301 first either way.
#24773 (MSVC SHA256 intrinsics) may be moot depending on the outcome of the MSVC-support question in #31507; resolve that before reviewing the patch.
result.notes: This category is dominated by long author-stacked chains (argsman, util::Result, logging macros/context, silent payments, multiprocess IPC). Bands were kept spread out: the few items with real corruption/crash consequences are P1, foundations whose dependents are themselves valuable are P2, and the many behaviour-neutral cleanups stay P3 even though internal work is the subject here. Within P2 and P3, dependency order was preserved so no base sits below its dependent.
